title: Wrestling Bout Between Miri Singh and Sangat Singh

blocks.text: Dohra:

One who acted as one of the arbitrators (during the factional dispute), Was named Lahora Singh from the community of kalals1 . The (defeated) Bandhayee Singhs sent him as their messenger, To resolve some issues with the (Tat Khalsa) Singhs. (1)
lines: One who acted as one of the arbitrators (during the factional dispute),
Was named Lahora Singh from the community of kalals1 .
The (defeated) Bandhayee Singhs sent him as their messenger,
To resolve some issues with the (Tat Khalsa) Singhs.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
The person who accompanied him was his own son, Who was known by the name of Sangat Singh.
Baba Kahan Singh disclosed it to Lahora Singh, That his (Tat Khalsa) Singhs were desperate to take on him. (2)
lines: Baba Kahan Singh disclosed it to Lahora Singh,
That his (Tat Khalsa) Singhs were desperate to take on him.

blocks.text: (Baba Kahan Singh) told that he was warning him in an advance, Lest the latter should allege that he was given no notice. Baba Kahan Singh, summoning his own son Miri Singh, Made him fight a wrestling bout with Sangat Singh, (Lahora Singh's son). (3)
lines: (Baba Kahan Singh) told that he was warning him in an advance,
Lest the latter should allege that he was given no notice.
Baba Kahan Singh, summoning his own son Miri Singh,
Made him fight a wrestling bout with Sangat Singh,
(Lahora Singh's son).

blocks.text: As both the youths were engaged in a wrestling bout, The two elders made a verbal promise with each other. That whosoever won would make the vanquished join his religious order, That was the agreement reached between the two elders. (4)
lines: As both the youths were engaged in a wrestling bout,
The two elders made a verbal promise with each other.
That whosoever won would make the vanquished join his religious order,
That was the agreement reached between the two elders.

blocks.text: Dohra:

While Miri Singh was the son of (Baba) Kahan Singh, Sangat Singh was Lahora Singh Kalal's son. While this wrestling bout was in progress near Akal Bunga, All the (Tat Khalsa) Singhs were witnessing this wrestling match. (5)
lines: While Miri Singh was the son of (Baba) Kahan Singh,
Sangat Singh was Lahora Singh Kalal's son.
While this wrestling bout was in progress near Akal Bunga,
All the (Tat Khalsa) Singhs were witnessing this wrestling match.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As soon as Miri Singh took the other's hand in his grip, Sangat Singh fell to the ground under the former's weight. Asking for a bowl of (pork) meat to be brought immediately, Miri Singh forced a piece of pork down Sangat Singh's throat. (6)
lines: As soon as Miri Singh took the other's hand in his grip,
Sangat Singh fell to the ground under the former's weight.
Asking for a bowl of (pork) meat to be brought immediately,
Miri Singh forced a piece of pork down Sangat Singh's throat.

blocks.text: Even as the son was converted to a Singh (from a non-vegetarian Bishnoi), Lahora Singh, the father, still remained to be brought to the Sikh fold. Lahora Singh stood humbled with folded hands before the Khalsa Singhs, Begging for an exemption from partaking of Non- vegetarian food. (7)
lines: Even as the son was converted to a Singh (from a non-vegetarian Bishnoi),
Lahora Singh, the father, still remained to be brought to the Sikh fold.
Lahora Singh stood humbled with folded hands before the Khalsa Singhs,
Begging for an exemption from partaking of Non- vegetarian food.

blocks.text: Now listen to the account of the chief of the Bandhayee Singhs, And the (brutal) manner in which he was slaughtered. When the Tat Khalsa Singhs asked him to vacate his camp, He refused, which led to a further strife between the two factions. (8)
lines: Now listen to the account of the chief of the Bandhayee Singhs,
And the (brutal) manner in which he was slaughtered.
When the Tat Khalsa Singhs asked him to vacate his camp,
He refused, which led to a further strife between the two factions.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the shouts for vengeance became louder from both the sides, There was a lot of violence and bloodshed all around. As the (Tat Khalsa) Singhs picked up their arms against Bandhayees, No body could dare to stop them from committing violence. (9)
lines: As the shouts for vengeance became louder from both the sides,
There was a lot of violence and bloodshed all around.
As the (Tat Khalsa) Singhs picked up their arms against Bandhayees,
No body could dare to stop them from committing violence.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The (Tat Khalsa) Singhs attacked the Bandayees with shouts of Akal2 , And dismantled the fence put up by the Bandhayee Singhs. As swords and other weapons struck from both the sides, The Bandhayee Singhs could not stand the Tat Khalsa attack. (10)
lines: The (Tat Khalsa) Singhs attacked the Bandayees with shouts of Akal2 ,
And dismantled the fence put up by the Bandhayee Singhs.
As swords and other weapons struck from both the sides,
The Bandhayee Singhs could not stand the Tat Khalsa attack.

blocks.text: The person who was made to occupy the Bandhayee chief's seat, Was slaughtered by the Khalsa Singhs after climbing up the podium. The cushioned throne which was put up on a wagon's platform, Was occupied by the invading Tat Khalsa Singhs on a wagon. (11)
lines: The person who was made to occupy the Bandhayee chief's seat,
Was slaughtered by the Khalsa Singhs after climbing up the podium.
The cushioned throne which was put up on a wagon's platform,
Was occupied by the invading Tat Khalsa Singhs on a wagon.

blocks.text: This Bandhayee chief who hailed from the town of Khemkaran3 , Belonged to the Community of Kambojs4 and named Mahant Singh. Those who did not surrender and lay down their arms, They were slaughtered and picked up in a heap by the Khalsa Singhs. (12)
lines: This Bandhayee chief who hailed from the town of Khemkaran3 ,
Belonged to the Community of Kambojs4 and named Mahant Singh.
Those who did not surrender and lay down their arms,
They were slaughtered and picked up in a heap by the Khalsa Singhs.

blocks.text: Those who surrendered and laid down their arms, They were spared and accepted into the Khalsa Panth. As the writ of Khalsa Panth ran large all around, Those alone survived who accepted "Waheguru ji ki Fateh" ideology. (13)
lines: Those who surrendered and laid down their arms,
They were spared and accepted into the Khalsa Panth.
As the writ of Khalsa Panth ran large all around,
Those alone survived who accepted "Waheguru ji ki Fateh" ideology.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As Khalsa Panth's writ ran large and overwhelmed everyone else, No Bandhayee Singh could survive Khalsa Panth's onslaught. A few old Bandhayee Singhs who had taken a temporary refuge, Also accepted defeat and merged with the Khalsa Panth. (14)
lines: As Khalsa Panth's writ ran large and overwhelmed everyone else,
No Bandhayee Singh could survive Khalsa Panth's onslaught.
A few old Bandhayee Singhs who had taken a temporary refuge,
Also accepted defeat and merged with the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The throne which was raised by the Bandhayee Singhs, Was made to be occupied by (the revered) Bhai Mani Singh5 . Whosoever surrendered and submitted to his authority, He was allowed to join the Khalsa Panth after undergoing the prescribed punishment.(15)
lines: The throne which was raised by the Bandhayee Singhs,
Was made to be occupied by (the revered) Bhai Mani Singh5 .
Whosoever surrendered and submitted to his authority,
He was allowed to join the Khalsa Panth after undergoing the prescribed punishment.

blocks.text: Nanu Singh from village Dhesian was among those who surrendered, Along with Lahora Singh and Shyam Singh from the wine sellers community. Bakhshish Singh was another who came into the Khalsa Panth, Who hailed from the village named Chamari (in Punjab). (16)
lines: Nanu Singh from village Dhesian was among those who surrendered,
Along with Lahora Singh and Shyam Singh from the wine sellers community.
Bakhshish Singh was another who came into the Khalsa Panth,
Who hailed from the village named Chamari (in Punjab).

blocks.text: Among the surrendered were two grandsons of Bhai Bhagtu6 , Who had been conferred the titles of Nawab by Banda Singh. The Khalsa Singhs, catching hold of all these renegades, Were made to don the blue robes of the Khalsa Panth. (17)
lines: Among the surrendered were two grandsons of Bhai Bhagtu6 ,
Who had been conferred the titles of Nawab by Banda Singh.
The Khalsa Singhs, catching hold of all these renegades,
Were made to don the blue robes of the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Dohra:

All the Bandhayee colleagues made a joint submission (to the Khalsa), That they had no objection to any proposal of the Singhs, Since a maid servant (a slave) was bound to follow her master's orders, She has to accept the dress code prescribed by her master. (18)
lines: All the Bandhayee colleagues made a joint submission (to the Khalsa),
That they had no objection to any proposal of the Singhs,
Since a maid servant (a slave) was bound to follow her master's orders,
She has to accept the dress code prescribed by her master.

blocks.text: This is how the encounter came to a final conclusion, Between the Bandhayee Singhs and the Tat Khalsa Singhs, Rattan Singh (the author) has recorded it in black and while, As he heard the whole account (from his own sources). (19)
lines: This is how the encounter came to a final conclusion,
Between the Bandhayee Singhs and the Tat Khalsa Singhs,
Rattan Singh (the author) has recorded it in black and while,
As he heard the whole account (from his own sources).
